sources.summary: Lists Muni buses, Metro, historic streetcars and cable cars, with journey-planning and accessibility resources.

sources.title: Airport Connections: SFO — BART
sources.summary: SFO station is in the International Terminal; AirTrain connects terminals. Current instructions describe contactless/Clipper options and using the same payment method at entry and exit.

sources.title: Transportation Basics — San Francisco Travel
sources.summary: Tourism-board overview of local and regional transportation. Used for general orientation, not exact fares or universal payment assertions.

sources.title: MuniMobile — SFMTA
sources.summary: September 1, 2026 ended sales of single-ride tickets in the app; some products remain during the phased retirement.

sources.title: Visitor Passports — SFMTA
sources.summary: Describes 1-, 3- and 7-day Muni coverage including cable cars, and excludes BART/airport transportation.

sources.title: Cable Cars — SFMTA
sources.summary: Lists California, Powell-Hyde and Powell-Mason lines and states that cable cars do not have accessible boarding.

sources.title: Accessibility for All — SFMTA
sources.summary: Links to accessible transit information and current Muni Metro elevator status; individual route suitability must be checked.

claims.claim: Muni includes buses, Metro, historic streetcars and cable cars.
BART connects SFO and downtown; airport station/terminal access instructions are published by BART.
BART currently describes contactless and Clipper options and requires the same payment method at entry and exit.
MuniMobile stopped selling single-ride tickets on September 1, 2026; products and transition details are changing.
Visitor Passports cover specified Muni services including cable cars, not BART or SFO airport transportation.
Three cable car lines are listed; cable cars do not offer accessible boarding.
SFMTA offers accessible transit and Metro elevator-status resources; suitability is journey-specific.

overlapReview: Reviewed existing 48-hour itinerary, lodging and scenic-view articles. They mention walking/cable cars but do not explain network selection, airport transfers or current payment/pass distinctions. This guide answers transport-planning intent and links to the itinerary rather than restating its stops.
limitations: No first-hand travel, tested routes, queue timings, fare quotes or guaranteed accessibility are claimed.
The SFMTA generic visitors page still promotes MuniMobile broadly; the dated MuniMobile service notice is treated as authoritative for changed ticket availability.
San Francisco Travel broadly describes tap-to-pay; detailed fare-use instructions are instead attributed to the operating agencies.
Official page retrieval is not an independent operational audit; all time-sensitive claims remain flagged for owner review.
